question: The expression \[\dfrac{2021}{2020} - \dfrac{2020}{2021}\] is equal to the fraction \(\frac{p}{q}\) in which \(p\) and \(q\) are positive integers whose greatest common divisor is \(1.\) What is \(p?\)
solution:
A common denominator produces a difference of consecutive squares, which factors without calculating either square:
\[
\frac{2021}{2020}-\frac{2020}{2021}
=\frac{2021^2-2020^2}{2020\cdot2021}
=\frac{(2021-2020)(2021+2020)}{2020\cdot2021}
=\frac{4041}{2020\cdot2021}.
\]
We must check that reducing the fraction will not change its numerator. Any common divisor of \(4041\) and \(2020\) divides
\[
4041-2\cdot2020=1.
\]
Similarly, any common divisor of \(4041\) and \(2021\) divides
\[
2\cdot2021-4041=1.
\]
Thus \(4041\) shares no prime factor with either factor of the denominator, so the fraction is already in lowest terms. Therefore \(p=\boxed{4041}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
The first fraction is just above \(1\), and the second is just below \(1\). Writing those differences explicitly avoids squaring:
\[
\frac{2021}{2020}=1+\frac1{2020},
\qquad
\frac{2020}{2021}=1-\frac1{2021}.
\]
Subtracting cancels the two \(1\)'s, leaving
\[
\frac1{2020}+\frac1{2021}
=\frac{2021+2020}{2020\cdot2021}
=\frac{4041}{2020\cdot2021}.
\]
To check lowest terms, suppose a prime divided both numerator and denominator. Because it divides the product \(2020\cdot2021\), it must divide at least one of those two factors. Since the numerator is their sum, it would then divide the other factor too. But a common divisor of consecutive integers divides their difference, \(1\), so no such prime exists.

The fraction is already reduced. Hence \(p=\boxed{4041}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
solutionMethods.label: Compare each fraction with 1
